title: DLP engines: the unit a rule references
aliases: can a dlp rule use my custom dictionary

prose.text: {{engine-definition}} {{rules-reference-engines}} {{api-rule-has-engines-only}} The dictionaries themselves are in [[zia.dlp.dictionaries]]; the rule side is in [[zia.dlp.rules]].

Terraform's handling of engines and rules has its own defects; see [[zia.terraform.field-fidelity]]. Managing custom engines through Terraform needs the write methods enabled by Support {{tf-custom-engine-writes-need-support}}.

checks.do: Whether the custom dictionary is in an engine, and whether that engine is on the rule, since a rule cannot reference a dictionary directly.
Whether the D<number> terms of an engine expression are resolved to dictionary IDs, since the engine object carries only the expression string.
Whether a channel-scoped engine triggers on web traffic, which a lab test would show.

engine-definition.statement: A DLP engine is a collection of one or more DLP dictionaries, and any mix of cloned, predefined and custom dictionaries can be added to one.

quotes: A Data Loss Prevention (DLP) engine is a collection of one or more DLP dictionaries.
Any combination of cloned, predefined, and custom dictionaries can be added to a DLP engine

rules-reference-engines.statement: DLP policy rules and Endpoint DLP policy rules must reference engines, not dictionaries. To use a custom dictionary in a rule, put it in an engine first.

quotes: When you define your DLP policy rules and Endpoint DLP policy rules, you must reference DLP engines, rather than DLP dictionaries.
which is what you must reference when creating DLP policies

api-rule-has-engines-only.statement: The Web DLP rule object carries a `dlpEngines` list and no field for dictionaries, so the indirection is an API-level requirement as well as a console one.
api-rule-has-engines-only.conditions: Rests on an absence in the Go SDK rule struct and the API reference's request fields for the add-rule operation: neither lists a dictionary field. Search: the field names of `request_body` for zia/data-loss-prevention/web-dlp-rule-resource-add-rule contain no name matching `dictionar`.

quotes: // The list of DLP engines to which the DLP policy rule must be applied.

predefined-engines-exist.statement: Zscaler provides predefined engines (the Match Only example names a PCI engine and a HIPAA engine) and supports custom ones. An admin can edit or clone a predefined engine as well as create a custom engine.

quotes: The Zscaler service provides predefined DLP engines and supports custom DLP engines.
You can edit predefined engines, create custom engines, or clone existing engines
For example, you create a DLP rule with the PCI engine and select the Match Only option. In this case, the rule does not trigger when a transaction triggers both the PCI and HIPAA engine.

boolean-composition.statement: An engine combines dictionaries with Boolean operators into a logical expression. The API expresses this as `engineExpression`, using All (AND), Any (OR), Exclude (NOT) and Sum (the total number of content matches).

quotes: you can also combine dictionaries with Boolean operators to create logical expressions

expression-wire-form.statement: On the wire an expression references dictionaries by ID, each wrapped in a `D` prefix and an `.S` suffix and compared with a number, for example `((D63.S > 1) AND (D38.S > 0))`. The engine object stores the expression as one string; it has no separate list of dictionaries.

quotes: // The boolean logical operator in which various DLP dictionaries are combined within a DLP engine's expression.

validate-expression-endpoint.statement: The API has an endpoint that validates an engine expression before it is saved.

engine-channels.statement: The DLP Engines page shows, per engine, the channels (Network Share, Personal Cloud Storage, Printing, or Removable Storage) associated with it. These are the Endpoint DLP channels.

quotes: Channels: The specific channels (Network Share, Personal Cloud Storage, Printing, or Removable Storage) associated with the DLP engine.

engine-limits.statement: A tenant can hold 480 custom engines with DLP Engine Expansion enabled and 58 without it.

quotes: | Custom DLP Engines | 480 engines (with DLP Engine Expansion enabled)58 engines (with DLP Engine Expansion disabled) |

tf-custom-engine-writes-need-support.statement: The Terraform `zia_dlp_engines` documentation says to contact Zscaler Support to have the POST, PUT and DELETE API methods enabled for the organization before using the resource.

quotes: request the following API methods ``POST``, ``PUT``, and ``DELETE`` to be enabled for your organization.

expression-threshold-meaning.title: What the number in a dictionary term such as D63.S > 1 compares against
expression-threshold-meaning.blocks: stating whether the engine threshold is a match count or a confidence score
expression-threshold-meaning.detail: The API describes Sum as the total number of content matches, which suggests the `.S` value is a match count, but no source defines `.S`. A help article on understanding DLP engines is referenced by the captured engines article but not captured.

channel-scoping-semantics.title: Whether a channel association limits where an engine triggers
channel-scoping-semantics.blocks: saying that a channel-scoped engine never fires on inline web traffic
channel-scoping-semantics.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "an engine can be scoped to specific channels ... engines scoped to them only trigger on that traffic type. Inline (web) DLP engines don't need channel scoping." The help page lists channels as a column on the engines table; no captured source says a channel association restricts an engine to that channel, or that an engine without channels is inline-only.

predefined-engine-regimes.title: Unverified legacy statement: predefined engines exist per regulation such as HIPAA, PCI and GDPR
predefined-engine-regimes.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Zscaler ships predefined engines (HIPAA, PCI, GDPR, etc.) that already combine multiple dictionaries per regulation." Only PCI, HIPAA and PII engines are named in help examples; GDPR and the per-regulation composition are not stated.

composite-example.title: Unverified legacy statement: example engine (CreditCards OR SSNs) AND Healthcare
composite-example.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "An engine can say '(CreditCards OR SSNs) AND Healthcare'". Illustrative only; replaced by the expression forms in the API reference (see boolean-composition).
